description: Cross-implementation vectors for the signed PWA bundle format v2. Generated by generate.mjs; see scripts/bundle-lib.mjs for the format.

format.bundleJson: {v:2, files:[{path,sha256,size}], manifestSha256, seq, builtAt, sig, pubkey}
format.manifestSha256: hex sha256 of JSON.stringify(files) (key order path, sha256, size)
format.order: depth-first directory walk, entries of each directory sorted by UTF-16 code units, root bundle.json skipped
format.filesOverride: base64 content by path applied on top of `files`; null removes the file; the served set must equal the manifest list, else hashMismatch

A.note: public test key, never use for anything real

B.note: public test key, never use for anything real

cases.name: valid
cases.why: the reference output: Rust must reproduce this bundle.json byte for byte from SITE + keyA + seq + builtAt

cases.name: valid-unpinned
cases.why: no pin: signature checked against the key inside the file

cases.name: valid-min-seq-equal
cases.why: seq equal to the stored maximum is accepted (only lower is a rollback)

cases.name: valid-empty-files
cases.why: an empty file list is well formed

cases.name: valid-seq-zero
cases.why: seq 0 is a valid integer

cases.name: valid-seq-max-safe
cases.why: seq 2^53-1 is the largest accepted value

cases.name: tamper-file-hash-in-manifest
cases.why: one hex digit of a file hash changed, manifestSha256 and sig untouched

cases.name: tamper-file-size-in-manifest
cases.why: a file size changed

cases.name: tamper-manifest-sha256
cases.why: manifestSha256 replaced by another well-formed digest

cases.name: tamper-file-and-manifest-hash
cases.why: attacker fixes manifestSha256 for a changed file list but cannot re-sign

cases.name: tamper-seq-up
cases.why: seq raised by one

cases.name: tamper-seq-down
cases.why: seq lowered by one

cases.name: tamper-sig-first-byte
cases.why: first signature byte flipped

cases.name: tamper-sig-last-byte
cases.why: last signature byte flipped

cases.name: tamper-sig-all-zero
cases.why: all-zero signature

cases.name: tamper-pubkey-unpinned
cases.why: pubkey replaced by key B without a pin: the signature no longer matches

cases.name: signed-by-other-key-pinned
cases.why: a correct bundle signed by key B while the phone pinned key A

cases.name: signed-by-other-key-unpinned
cases.why: same bundle without a pin verifies (this is why the pin is the root of trust)

cases.name: pubkey-swapped-and-resigned-pinned
cases.why: attacker swaps the pubkey field to its own and re-signs; the pin catches it

cases.name: small-order-key-forgery-pinned
cases.why: identity-point public key with the trivial signature R=identity,S=0; only the pin stops it

cases.name: rollback
cases.why: correctly signed but older than the highest seq the phone accepted

cases.name: rollback-old-signed-build
cases.why: an old build signed with the same key

cases.name: v1-refused
cases.why: format v1 (signature over the bare manifest hash) is refused by default

cases.name: v1-allowed-in-tests
cases.why: with allowV1 the legacy bundle verifies (tests only)

cases.name: v1-signature-relabelled-v2
cases.why: a v1 signature copied into a v2 manifest: domain separation makes it fail

cases.name: v1-signature-with-v2-label-no-seq
cases.why: v:2 without a seq

cases.name: wrong-domain-string
cases.why: signature over the right fields with another domain prefix

cases.name: missing-separator
cases.why: signature over domain+hash+seq without the newline before seq

cases.name: signature-over-bare-hash
cases.why: signature over the manifest hash alone (the v1 message) in a v2 manifest

cases.name: malleated-signature-s-plus-l
cases.why: S replaced by S+L: a strict verifier must reject the non-canonical scalar

cases.name: seq-string
cases.why: seq as a string

cases.name: seq-float
cases.why: seq 1.5

cases.name: seq-negative
cases.why: seq -1

cases.name: seq-2-pow-53
cases.why: seq 2^53 is not a safe integer

cases.name: seq-null
cases.why: seq null

cases.name: path-parent-traversal

cases.name: path-embedded-traversal
